title: Schema relaxation + constrained-sampling policy experiments for noisy streaming outputs
creator: Maya Chen
description: Investigate and validate a pragmatic approach to schema adherence for streaming JSON mode responses under noisy/partial tokens. Goal: reduce brittle failures from strict decoders by combining schema relaxation heuristics with a constrained-sampling policy that prefers schema-compliant token sequences while retaining deterministic fallback behavior.
test_plan: Create synthetic streaming responses with common noise modes (truncated-object, extra-commas, invalid-escapes, partial-utf8, interleaved tool-call tokens).
Implement constrained-sampling shim that can be enabled per-request: enforces allowed-token-lists at the decoder boundary and biases top-k to schema-safe tokens when ambiguity detected.
Run end-to-end integration runs across CPU- and GPU-backed runtime variants and both streaming and non-streaming endpoints.
Measure incidence of schema-failure exceptions, successful auto-recovery (post-stream fixups), latency overhead, and token-cost delta compared to baseline strict-decoder behavior.
test_cases: TC-01 truncated-object: stream stops mid-object; decoder should return best-effort parse and mark 'partial' flag in metadata
TC-02 comma-noise: extra commas inserted between items; permissive profile should accept and normalize output
TC-03 escape-garbage: broken string escapes in streaming chunks; constrained sampler should avoid tokens that produce invalid escapes
TC-04 tool-call-interleaving: tool/function-call markers interleaved; decoder must preserve tool-call boundaries and produce valid JSON around calls
TC-05 recovery-rollforward: simulate low-latency recovery where runtime patches the KV-cache and replays remaining tokens to fix schema violations
acceptance_criteria: Reduction of schema-failure exceptions by >= 85% for permissive profile on noisy synthetic corpus compared to strict baseline
Median additional latency for constrained-sampling path <= 12ms at 95th percentile under typical request sizes
Fallback deterministic behavior: when constrained-sampling is disabled, old strict-decoder behavior is preserved
Clear telemetry events emitted for: schema-relaxation-mode, sampler-bias-applied, recovery-attempted, recovery-succeeded/failed
Automated contract tests added to CI for all test cases above and gated for runtime-2.1 release
observations: Initial alpha runs show constrained-sampling reduces invalid-escape cases by 92% but increases average token-entropy slightly.
Streaming microbenchmarks reveal a CPU-side 6-9ms overhead when applying token-level allow-lists; GPU decode unaffected.
Permissive profile prevented 78% of truncated-object error reports coming from customer-facing deployments in a 24h A/B run.
Edge case: interleaved tool-call tokens cause parser confusion when tool-call markers are emitted across chunk boundaries; requires marker anchoring in sampler.
dev_notes: Prototype implemented as a decoder-wrapper, feature-flagged via request.query['schema_profile'].
Constrained-sampling uses a three-state bias: allow-only (hard mask), soft-bias (boost scores), and none. Tunable per-schema-field via a small JSON policy table.
We instrumented metrics: schema_profile, sampler_mode, sampler_overrides_count, recovery_attempts, recovery_latency_ms.
